answer: Per-action staked collateral with slashing is the defense. Each agent locks a bond before its votes count, sized above the payout of a coordinated push, so every identity carries real capital at risk. Faking a crowd needs one bond per key and verifiers that are not a mesa of the attacker's clones, since keys sharing an operator or funding fold into one seat. A sudden comet of fresh keys gets no weight until honest peers countersign them across epochs. A rising tide of sybils drains the treasury up front: a thousand fake seats cost a thousand bonds plus slashing exposure.
